title: Write a Health-Check Script: Arrays, Functions, Loops, and trap
intro: The earlier bash labs were straight-line scripts. Real automation loops over lists, factors repeated logic into functions, cleans up after itself even when it fails, and reports a meaningful exit code. Write a script that checks a list of service URLs and says which ones are down.

steps.starter_content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Check each service URL and report which are down.
steps.prompt:
Write healthcheck.sh:
(1) 'set -euo pipefail'.
(2) Create a temp file with tmp=$(mktemp) and remove it on exit, even on error, with: trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
(3) An array: urls=("http://api:8080/health" "http://web:3000/health")
(4) A function check_url() that stores its argument in a 'local' variable and runs curl -fsS --max-time 5 on it, sending output to "$tmp" and returning curl's status.
(5) failures=0, then loop with for url in "${urls[@]}"; do ... done. For each URL, if check_url succeeds, print 'OK <url>'. Otherwise print 'DOWN <url>' to stderr and increment the counter with failures=$((failures + 1)).
(6) End with exit "$failures" so the exit code is the number of services down.
steps.hint: Order: set -euo pipefail, then tmp=$(mktemp) and the trap, then the urls=(...) array, then the function (check_url() { local url="$1"; curl -fsS --max-time 5 "$url" > "$tmp"; }), then the loop (inside it, use 'if check_url "$url"; then ... else ... fi'), then exit "$failures". Don't use ((failures++)): see the 'why' after you pass.
steps.solution:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Check each service URL and report which are down.
set -euo pipefail

tmp=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

urls=("http://api:8080/health" "http://web:3000/health")

check_url() {
  local url="$1"
  curl -fsS --max-time 5 "$url" > "$tmp"
}

failures=0
for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
  if check_url "$url"; then
    echo "OK   $url"
  else
    echo "DOWN $url" >&2
    failures=$((failures + 1))
  fi
done

exit "$failures"
steps.fake_output:
$ ./healthcheck.sh
OK   http://api:8080/health
curl: (7) Failed to connect to web port 3000: Connection refused
DOWN http://web:3000/health
$ echo $?
1
steps.explanation: Checks every URL even when one fails, reports on the right streams, cleans up its temp file on any exit, and exits with the failure count.
steps.why: Several deliberate choices here. (1) Calling check_url inside 'if' is what keeps 'set -e' from killing the script at the first down service: commands tested by if/while/&&/|| are exempt from -e. (2) ((failures++)) is a classic -e trap: when failures is 0, the expression evaluates to 0, which bash treats as a failing status, so the script exits on the very first failure. $((failures + 1)) in an assignment always succeeds. (3) "${urls[@]}" with quotes expands to one word per element, even if a URL contains spaces; unquoted, it word-splits. (4) trap ... EXIT runs on normal exit, on error, and on Ctrl+C, so temp files and lock files never leak. (5) 'local' keeps the function's variables from overwriting globals of the same name. (6) curl -f turns HTTP 4xx/5xx into a failing exit code, which curl doesn't do by default, and --max-time stops one hung service from hanging the whole check.
